title: Phones, computers and the internet
intro: This is the one area where borrowed English is normal and understood everywhere, but the native words are still the ones printed on signs and menus. Both are given.

entries.note: el celular in Latin America, el móvil in Spain. Both mean mobile phone.

ex.es: Se me quedó el teléfono en casa.
ex.en: I left my phone at home.

entries.note: la computadora in Latin America, el ordenador in Spain. Both are everyday.

ex.en: The computer is running very slowly.

entries.note: Also the cinema screen and a lampshade.

ex.es: Se rompió la pantalla del celular.
ex.en: The phone screen broke.

entries.note: la tecla is a single key; el ratón the mouse.

ex.es: El teclado no tiene la eñe.
ex.en: The keyboard doesn't have an ñ.
I can't open the file.

ex.es: Lo encontré en el archivo nacional.
ex.en: I found it in the national archive.

entries.en: to save; to keep, to put away

ex.es: Guarda el archivo antes de cerrar.
ex.en: Save the file before closing.

ex.es: Guarda la ropa en el cajón.
ex.en: Put the clothes away in the drawer.

entries.en: to delete, to erase, to rub out

ex.en: I deleted the message without reading it.

entries.note: la clave is used just as often, and also means key or code.

ex.en: I've forgotten the password again.

entries.note: las redes sociales is social media. la Red with a capital is the internet.

ex.es: No hay red en este cuarto.
ex.en: There's no signal in this room.

ex.es: La pelota pasó por encima de la red.
ex.en: The ball went over the net.

entries.note: el correo electrónico in full; everyone says el correo. la oficina de correos is the post office.

ex.en: I sent you an email yesterday.
It came in the post this morning.

entries.note: el vínculo is the formal word. Many people just say el link.

ex.en: Click on the link.

entries.note: bajar does the job too — see unit 22.

ex.en: I downloaded the film last night.
They're unloading the lorry.

entries.note: Same verb as to go up — see unit 22. Context decides.

ex.es: Subió las fotos a la nube.
ex.en: She uploaded the photos to the cloud.
The system has a thousand users.
Type your username and password.

entries.note: Often shortened to la app, pronounced as in English.

ex.en: That app uses a lot of battery.

entries.note: la pila is a small battery, the AA kind.

ex.en: My battery died.

ex.es: Toca la batería en un grupo.
ex.en: He plays drums in a band.

entries.en: to charge; to carry, to load

ex.en: I need to charge my phone.

ex.es: Cargó las bolsas hasta el carro.
ex.en: He carried the bags to the car.

entries.note: Used of machines, never of people. For people, trabajar.

ex.en: The remote doesn't work.

entries.en: to switch on; to switch off
entries.note: prender is the Latin American everyday word for on; encender is standard everywhere.

ex.en: Switch the computer on.

ex.es: Apaga el teléfono en el cine.
ex.en: Switch your phone off in the cinema.

entries.note: Short for la fotografía, and feminine even though it ends in -o. tomar or sacar una foto is to take a photo.

ex.en: Would you take a photo of us?
